article.headline: Lightning storm back from 2-goal deficit to beat the Canucks 4-2
article.description: — Nikita Kucherov scored twice, Jake Guentzel had a goal and an assist, and Dennis Hildeby stopped 12 shots as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the Vancouver Canucks 4-2 on Saturday.

article.story: TAMPA, Fla. -- — Nikita Kucherov scored twice, Jake Guentzel had a goal and an assist, and Dennis Hildeby stopped 12 shots as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the Vancouver Canucks 4-2 on Saturday. Guentzel scored the winner in the third period as Tampa Bay came back from a two-goal deficit. Pontus Holmberg also scored and Brayden Point finished with two assists for Tampa Bay, which improved to 5-0 at home. Linus Karlsson and Elias Pettersson scored while Kevin Lankinen finished with 31 saves for the Canucks, who finished winless (0-4-1) on a five-game road trip. Vancouver is winless in the past seven games (0-6-1) overall. Guentzel picked up the winner at 2:04 of the third after Charle-Edouard D'Astous slid a pass off the wall to Guentzel for the quick snap shot that deflected off the stick of Vancouver's Liam Ohgren. For the second consecutive game, the Canucks had a 2-0 lead they were not able to hold. Karlsson put Vancouver up 1-0 at 15:32 of the first period with a shot from the right point. Pettersson put the Canucks up 2-0 with a power-play goal at 4:35 of the second period. Kucherov scored twice in the span of 4:53 to pull the Lightning even. He scored his first goal off his own rebound on the power play at 6:30. Kucherov scored again as Point pulled a faceoff back to Kucherov for the quick shot at 11:23. Holmberg capped the scoring, getting to a loose puck off a faceoff and beating Lankinen through the pads at 15:57. Up next Canucks: Host the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday night. Lightning: Travel to face the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NHL coverage here
